articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: CISA — the agency that's supposed to protect America's cyber infrastructure — just leaked their own AWS keys on GitHub like a first-year CS student. The irony is so thick you could cut it with a rusty server rack.

articles.title: Laravel-Lang PHP Packages Compromised to Deliver Cross-Platform Credential Stealer
articles.summary: Anthropic's Claude AI just casually found 10,000+ critical vulnerabilities in widely-used software in its first month of operation. Meanwhile, human security researchers are updating their résumés and questioning their life choices.

articles.title: Project Glasswing identifies over 10,000 critical vulnerabilities in first month using AI
articles.summary: LiteSpeed cPanel plugin gets a perfect 10.0 CVSS score for letting attackers run scripts as root — because apparently someone thought privilege escalation should be a feature, not a bug.

articles.title: GitHub Confirms 3,800 Internal Repos Stolen Through Poisoned VS Code Extension
articles.summary: TeamPCP is poisoning open source code at industrial scale, turning the commons into their personal malware distribution network. Supply chain attacks are the new black, and apparently everyone's wearing it.

articles.title: Project Glasswing: An Initial Update
articles.summary: GitHub confirms 3,800 internal repos got yoinked via poisoned VS Code extension — because even the code repository overlords fall for basic social engineering. The house always wins, until it doesn't.

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF celebrates a rare win for end-to-end encryption, because in 2026 we apparently still need to explain why private conversations should stay private. Democracy dies in plaintext, folks.

articles.title: Your Privacy Shouldn't Be A Corporate Decision
articles.summary: Microsoft actually took a step toward human rights accountability in their cloud services — shocking absolutely no one more than Microsoft themselves. Google and Amazon are reportedly checking their calendars for when hell freezes over.

articles.title: Akamai Joins Growing Chorus of Vendors Betting Big on Secure Enterprise Browsers
articles.summary: EFF drops a new guide on fighting digital surveillance abuses because apparently we need instruction manuals for basic human dignity. The panopticon won't dismantle itself, unfortunately.

articles.title: Cisco used AI to write security incident reports, with mixed results
articles.summary: Trump Mobile website allegedly leaked thousands of customers' personal data to anyone who could craft an HTTP request. MAGA meets GDPR violations — truly the crossover episode nobody asked for.

articles.title: AI Agents Are Shifting Identity Security Budget Dynamics
articles.summary: Google's API keys stay active for 23 minutes after 'deletion' despite claiming immediate removal — because in Google time, 'immediate' apparently means 'whenever we get around to it.'
